nodes.label: Developer
nodes.role: Pushes a feature branch and opens a pull request. Gets build failures and deploy notices in Slack.
nodes.was: Pushed to GitHub and got a Jenkins email when a build failed.
nodes.why: Slack messages arrive where the team already works and link straight to the failing step.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.role: Holds the application code and runs the ci.yml workflow. Branch protection requires every check to pass before merge.
nodes.was: A GitHub repo that Jenkins pulled from.
nodes.why: Required status checks stop failing or unreviewed code from reaching main.

nodes.label: Gitleaks
nodes.role: Scans every commit for API keys, passwords and tokens before anything is built.
nodes.why: A leaked AWS key is the most common way demo accounts get abused.

nodes.label: SonarQube
nodes.role: Static analysis for bugs and security hotspots. The quality gate fails the run if coverage drops or new issues appear.
nodes.why: Kept, and now a required pull request check with a hard gate.

nodes.label: Maven build
nodes.role: Compiles the Java service, runs the unit tests and produces the JAR.
nodes.was: Jenkins built and tested the JAR.
nodes.why: Kept, with Maven dependency caching between runs.

nodes.label: Docker Buildx
nodes.role: Builds a multi-stage image on a minimal Java runtime for both amd64 and arm64.
nodes.was: A single-stage Docker build in Jenkins.
nodes.why: Smaller images with no build tools inside. arm64 lets the cluster use cheaper Graviton nodes.

nodes.label: Trivy
nodes.role: Scans the image for known CVEs and the Terraform for misconfigurations. A CRITICAL finding stops the run before the image is pushed.
nodes.why: Vulnerable images never reach the registry.

nodes.label: Cosign + Syft
nodes.role: Signs the image with the workflow's OIDC identity (no key to manage) and attaches a software bill of materials.
nodes.why: The cluster can prove an image came from this pipeline and was not pushed by hand.

nodes.label: Amazon ECR
nodes.role: Private image registry with scan on push, immutable tags and lifecycle rules that delete old images.
nodes.was: Amazon ECR and Docker Hub side by side.
nodes.why: One registry inside AWS: no Docker Hub rate limits and one less credential to store.

nodes.label: Slack
nodes.role: Receives build failures from GitHub Actions, deploy status from Argo CD and runtime alerts from Alertmanager.
nodes.why: Build, deploy and runtime events land in one channel.

nodes.label: Platform engineer
nodes.role: Changes infrastructure only through pull requests to the Terraform code.
nodes.was: Created the Kubernetes cluster by hand with eksctl.
nodes.why: Every infrastructure change is reviewed, repeatable and reversible.

nodes.label: Terraform
nodes.role: Provisions the VPC, EKS, RDS, ECR, IAM and DNS. GitHub Actions runs plan on the pull request and apply on merge. State is stored in S3 with locking.
nodes.was: Not in the design; the cluster was created manually.
nodes.why: The platform can be rebuilt or destroyed with one command, which also keeps demo costs low.

nodes.label: Argo Rollouts
nodes.role: Moves traffic to the new version in steps and checks error rate and latency in Prometheus at each step. Rolls back on its own if they get worse.
nodes.was: All pods were replaced at once.
nodes.why: A bad release reaches 10% of users for a few minutes instead of everyone.

nodes.label: Kyverno
nodes.role: Rejects unsigned images, :latest tags, privileged pods and pods without resource limits.
nodes.why: The cluster enforces the rules, so nobody has to remember them.

nodes.label: Argo CD
nodes.role: Watches the GitOps repo and syncs the cluster to match it. Reverts manual changes automatically.
nodes.was: Jenkins pulled the image into the cluster directly.
nodes.why: Pull-based delivery means CI never holds cluster credentials.

nodes.label: GitOps repo
nodes.role: Holds the Helm chart and one values file per environment. CI commits the new image digest; prod is promoted by pull request.
nodes.why: Git becomes the record of exactly what runs where.

nodes.label: Users
nodes.role: Reach the app at app.example.com. Replace with your own domain.
nodes.why: Kept.

nodes.label: Route 53
nodes.role: DNS for the domain with health checks. ExternalDNS in the cluster keeps the records in sync.
nodes.was: Route 53 pointed straight at the cluster.
nodes.why: Kept, with records managed from Kubernetes.

nodes.label: CloudFront + WAF
nodes.role: Caches static content close to users. AWS WAF blocks common attacks and bad bots. TLS certificates come from ACM.
nodes.why: Protection and speed before a request reaches the cluster.

nodes.label: Load balancer
nodes.role: An Application Load Balancer created from the Kubernetes Ingress by the AWS Load Balancer Controller.
nodes.why: Routing is defined in Git next to the app.

nodes.label: Amazon EKS
nodes.role: Runs the service in private subnets across three availability zones. The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler adds pods under load.
nodes.was: A cluster created with eksctl, with Prometheus and Grafana inside it.
nodes.why: Same engine, now built by Terraform with managed add-ons and upgraded on a schedule.

nodes.label: RDS MySQL
nodes.role: MySQL with a standby in a second availability zone, encrypted with KMS, reachable only from the cluster's security group.
nodes.why: Kept, with Multi-AZ and automated backups. Aurora MySQL is the next step up.

nodes.label: Karpenter
nodes.role: Adds and removes nodes in seconds based on pending pods, preferring spot and Graviton instances.
nodes.why: You pay for the capacity the pods actually need.

nodes.label: Pod Identity
nodes.role: Gives each service account its own IAM role, so pods get short-lived AWS credentials.
nodes.was: Service accounts mapped to IAM roles (IRSA).
nodes.why: EKS Pod Identity is simpler to set up. IRSA still works if you prefer it.

nodes.label: Secrets Manager
nodes.role: Stores the database password with automatic rotation. External Secrets Operator syncs it into a Kubernetes Secret.
nodes.was: Pods read AWS Secrets Manager through IAM.
nodes.why: Passwords rotate without redeploying the app.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry
nodes.role: Collects metrics, logs and traces from the pods and forwards each to its store.
nodes.why: One vendor-neutral agent instead of several.

nodes.label: Prometheus
nodes.role: Stores metrics and evaluates alert rules. Alertmanager routes alerts to Slack. Argo Rollouts reads it for canary checks.
nodes.why: Kept, now with alert rules, routing and canary analysis.

nodes.label: Loki + Tempo
nodes.role: Loki stores logs and Tempo stores traces, both searchable from Grafana.
nodes.why: Go from a slow request to its trace and logs in one click.

nodes.label: Grafana
nodes.role: Dashboards for service health, SLOs and DORA metrics: deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate and recovery time.
nodes.why: DORA metrics show what the pipeline is worth in numbers people understand.
